newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends easier, gilt prices mixed.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends easier, gilt prices mixed.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday easier at 4.5 percent against opening quotes of 4.75-5.25 percent, dealers said.
They said good supply of funds and moderate demand pushed rates down.
"Lenders initially quoted higher rates...above five percemt," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But they lowered rates soon as there were no borrowers at higher levels."
Dealers said they expected rates to firm up marginally later in the week.
"There is a repo auction tomorrow," said a dealer. "Even though payments are made on Friday, there may be see some slight hardening in rates tomorrow."
He said rates could be firm next week as there were only two working days in which to cover positions.
Banks are closed on Monday and Friday and will report their positions to the central bank on Thursday.
Dealers said prices of government securities were ended mixed in brisk trade. Trades on the National Stock Exchange were worth 2.15 billion against Tuesday's 1.25 billion, they said.

"But volumes are still no really heavy," said a dealer. "There seems to be a mood of uncertainty prevailing among market operators. No one is sure how liquidity will be over the next week and this is restricting trade."

The 12 percent 1999 government of India stock traded on Wednesday at 100.01 rupees unchanged from its last traded price while the 13.50 percent 1997 eased to 101.40 from 101.43, dealers said. The 13.65 percent 1998 rose to 102.51 from 102.48.
The treasury bill maturing on October 10 yielded 10.10 percent, they said.
